rules.title: San Francisco allowable annual rent increase (1.6% for 3/1/2026–2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, the allowable annual rent increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%. Earlier periods: 1.4% for 2025–26 and 1.7% for 2024–25.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits. This page does not describe coverage.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate (4.2% for 3/1/2026–2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: San Francisco landlords must pay interest on security deposits. The rate is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods: 5.0% for 2025–26 and 5.2% for 2024–25.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposits on San Francisco residential rentals. This page does not describe coverage.

rules.title: Relocation payments for owner/relative move-in, demolition/removal, temporary capital improvement and substantial rehabilitation evictions
rules.requirement: If you are evicted for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work (20 days or more), or substantial rehabilitation, and the notice is served between 3/1/26 and 2/28/27, the landlord owes $8,245 per tenant, up to $24,733 per unit. The landlord also owes $5,497 more for each tenant who is elderly (60 or older) or disabled, and for each household with minor children.
rules.key_value: $8,245 per tenant; max $24,733 per unit; +$5,497 per elderly (60+)/disabled tenant or household with minor children (notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants who are served a termination notice on these no-fault grounds under the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 instead.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

rules.title: Ellis Act eviction relocation payments
rules.requirement: If you are evicted under the Ellis Act and the notice is served between 3/1/26 and 2/28/27, the landlord owes $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit. The landlord also owes $7,443.90 more for each tenant who is elderly (62 or older) or disabled.
rules.key_value: $11,110.05 per tenant; max $33,330.13 per unit; +$7,443.90 per elderly (62+)/disabled tenant (notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants served termination notices because the owner is withdrawing the units from the rental market under the Ellis Act.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation payments for tenants evicted under the Ellis Act

rules.title: Relocation payments for temporary displacement under 20 days (capital improvement)
rules.requirement: If you are temporarily displaced for less than 20 days for capital improvement work in San Francisco, the landlord owes $446.00 per day per tenant household, plus actual moving expenses, for notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27.
rules.key_value: $446.00/day per household plus actual moving expenses (notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in San Francisco rent-controlled units temporarily displaced for less than 20 days for capital improvement work.
rules.quoted_span: *The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.conflict_note: Displacements of less than 20 days are governed by the state statute, not by local S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C. The state law governs this subset.

notes: This is the SF Rent Board's rates page. It gives annual amounts, not the full legal rules. Citations: § 37.9C and § 37.9A are taken from the document, and Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 is cited in it. § 37.3(a)(1) (annual increase) and Admin. Code ch. 49 (deposit interest) come from outside knowledge, not the document. Coverage fields are left blank because the page does not state them. Under the Rent Ordinance, rent control generally covers units with a certificate of occupancy on or before 6/13/1979, but that is also not stated here. Left out: capital improvement imputed interest and labor rates (passthrough calculation details) and the Rent Board fee. Whether the $446/day figure for stays under 20 days was set by the Rent Board or by the state statute is not clear from the page.
